extraction_notes.note: Objects used by Lemmas 4.1, 5.1 and 5.2 (N_{2,n}, eta, hat g, Y_{i,n}) are defined in numbered equations inside the prose proofs of Theorems 2.1/2.2, part I. Since a proof stands for its theorem, these definitional \ref edges closed result cycles (TP2 -> LP2 -> LP3 -> TP2). The rules give no case for this, so I marked those edges, and the step-level 'as in Theorem 2.2' refs, as mention: true. The cycle comes from layout; the argument is not circular.

Appendix equations (A.2) and (A.4) are cited results of Strasser (Lemma 55.4, Corollary 59.6), so I retyped them as external theorems rather than equations. The Le Cam distance equation (A.3) stays inside a definition.

These are roadmap paragraphs that open Sections 4 and 5. I could have made them part of the proofs, but they contain no argument, so I typed them as remarks and gave them mention edges to the results they announce.

The proofs of Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 run as prose across subsections, with the auxiliary lemmas stated and proved in between. I emitted one proof node per part, each with a proves edge, and gave the continuation a uses edge to the first part.

Section 2.3 gives Monte Carlo evidence (Tables 1-3: likelihood-ratio quantiles and Wilcoxon tests). I captured only the verbal conclusion, as a claim with rigor numerical. The tables themselves are not nodes.

Not extracted: the introduction and conclusion summaries, the discussion of practical volatility estimation in Section 2.4 (Hubalek-Posedel and others), the description of the simulation design, and the interpretive sentence after the epsilon-deficiency definition in the Appendix.

The source has small notational slips. Part I of the proof of Theorem 2.2 cites N_n 'as in (defNn)', but that equation defines N_{1,n}. Part II of the proof of Theorem 2.1 writes theta=(h_0,beta,alpha,gamma). Statements are copied verbatim.

\end{eqnarray}

Kallsen and Vesenmayer \cite{KV07} have shown that
$(G_n[n\cdot],h_n[n\cdot])$, as defined in (\ref{G1}) by
$H_n(\theta)=H^{\mathrm{(KV)}}_n(\theta)$, converge to COGARCH with parameter
$\theta$ in (\ref{COG}) in law, with respect to the Skorokhod topology,
as $n\to\infty$, for all $\theta\in\Theta$.

Maller \textit{et al.} \cite{MMS08} have encountered a slightly different
scenario. For $\theta\in\Theta,$ they have embedded a sequence of GARCH
models into a given COGARCH and obtained the convergence with respect
to the same topology, now driven by a general L\'{e}vy process, even in
probability. If the driving process is a compound Poisson process with
rate $\gamma$ and jump size distribution $Q$, then their analysis
relates to a situation where the corresponding partial sums have the
same law as $(G_n[n\cdot],h_n[n\cdot])$ under the parametrization
$H^{\mathrm{(M)}}_n(\theta)$, $\theta\in\Theta$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

$\theta\in\Theta$, the partial sum
processes of GARCH with parametrization $H^{(KV)}_n(\theta)$ converge to
COGARCH in law, as
$n\to\infty$, with a similar result being true for the parametrization
$H^{(M)}_n(\theta)$ in~\cite{MMS08}. On the other hand,
both parametrizations fall into the framework of Theorem \ref{th2a}.
Hence, if the distribution of the innovations admits a Lebesgue
density, then the limiting experiment is given by MCOGARCH $\widehat
{\mathcal E}(\Theta)$ rather than COGARCH

threshold. Under reasonable assumptions, $Q_n$ converge weakly to a
generalized Pareto distribution~$Q$ as $n\to\infty$. Also, the
corresponding GARCH models converge in distribution in law to a COGARCH
driven by a compound Poisson process with jump distribution $Q$. In

law} if we are interested in the extreme parts of the innovations. On
the other hand, if $Q_n$ converges to $Q$, even in total variation

Suppose that (\ref{lre}) is satisfied for $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $p_n\in(0,1)$ and
$\gamma\in(0,\infty)$. Let $B_{n,1}, \dots,B_{n,n}$ be independent
Bernoulli variables with parameter $p_n$. Suppose that
$(U_k,\zeta_{n,k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ is an i.i.d. sequence of random vectors
with independent components, where~$U_k$ is uniformly distributed on
$(0,1)$ and ${\mathcal L}(\zeta_{n,k})=Q_n$. Suppose that $B_{n,1}, \dots,
B_{n,n}$ and $(U_k,\zeta_{n,k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ are independent. Observe
that

\[
{\mathcal L}(N_{2,n}) = {\mathcal L} \Biggl(\sum_{k=1}^n B_{n,k} \varepsilon
_{(V_{n,k},\zeta_{n,k})} \Biggr)
\]

with $V_{n,k}=(k - 1+ U_k)/n$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and\vspace*{1pt} $1\le k\le n$.

Let $\widehat N_n$ be a Poisson measure on $[0,1]\otimes\mathbb{R}$ with
intensity measure $np_n\ell\otimes Q_n$ and define

\[
\widehat N_{n,k}(B)=\widehat N_n \biggl(B\cap \biggl( \biggl(\frac{k -
1}n,\frac kn \biggr]\times\mathbb{R} \biggr) \biggr),\qquad  B\in{\mathcal B}
([0,1]\times\mathbb{R}) .
\]

$\widehat N_{n,1},\dots,\widehat N_{n,n}$ are then independent Poisson
point processes, where for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, \mbox{$1\le k\le n$}, $\widehat
N_{n,k}$ has intensity measure

\[
n p_n[\ell\otimes Q_n]  \biggl(B\cap \biggl( \biggl(\frac{k -
1}n,\frac kn \biggr]\times\mathbb{R} \biggr) \biggr),\qquad
  B\in{\mathcal B}([0,1]\times\mathbb{R}) .
\]

By the monotonicity theorem for
Markov kernels (see \cite{Re93}, Lemma 1.4.2(i)), observe that for all
$n\in\mathbb{N}$,


\begin{equation}\label{thin1}
\|{\mathcal L}(N_{2,n})-{\mathcal L}(\widehat N_n)\|
\le
 \Biggl\|\bigotimes_{k=1}^n{\mathcal L} \bigl(B_{n,k}
\varepsilon_{(V_{n,k},\zeta_{n,k})} \bigr)-\bigotimes_{k=1}^n{\mathcal L}
 (\widehat
N_{n,k}  ) \Biggr\| .
\end{equation}

Denote the Hellinger distance
between two probability measures $P_1$ and $P_2$ by $H(P_1,P_2)$. This
gives us the following upper bound (see \cite{Re93}, Section~1.3,
equation (1.23), and Section~1.3, equation (1.25)):


\begin{eqnarray}\label{thin2}
&&\Biggl\|\bigotimes_{k=1}^n{\mathcal L} \bigl(B_{n,k}
\varepsilon_{(V_{n,k},\zeta_{n,k})} \bigr)-\bigotimes_{k=1}^n{\mathcal L}
 (\widehat N_{n,k}) \Biggr\|\nonumber\\
&&\quad\le H \Biggl(\bigotimes_{k=1}^n{\mathcal L} \bigl(B_{n,k}
\varepsilon_{(V_{n,k},\zeta_{n,k})} \bigr),
\bigotimes_{k=1}^n{\mathcal L} (\widehat N_{n,k}) \Biggr)\\
&&\quad\le \Biggl(\sum_{k=1}^n H^2 \bigl({\mathcal L} \bigl(B_{n,k}
\varepsilon_{(V_{n,k},\zeta_{n,k})} \bigr),{\mathcal L} (\widehat
N_{n,k} ) \bigr) \Biggr)^{1/2}.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}

Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $1\le k\le n$. Let
$(V_{n,k,l},\zeta_{n,k,l})_{l\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of random
vectors with ${\mathcal L}(V_{n,k,l},\zeta_{n,k,l})={\mathcal L}(V_{n,k})\otimes Q_n$,
$l\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that $(V_{n,k,l})$ is independent of $B_{n,k}$ and
$\tau_{n,k}$, where $\tau_{n,k}$ is a Poisson\vadjust{\goodbreak} variable with parameter
$p_n$. We then have the following identities:

\[
{\mathcal L} \bigl(B_{n,k}
\varepsilon_{(V_{n,k},\zeta_{n,k})} \bigr)   =
{\mathcal L} \Biggl(\sum_{l=1}^{B_{n,k}}
\varepsilon_{(V_{n,k,l},\zeta_{n,k,l})} \Biggr),\qquad  {\mathcal L}
(\widehat N_{n,k})   =   {\mathcal L} \Biggl(\sum_{l=1}^{\tau_{n,k}}
\varepsilon_{(V_{n,k,l},\zeta_{n,k,l})} \Biggr) .
\]

By \cite{Re93}, Lemma 1.4.2(ii), for $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $1\le k\le n$, we
must have


\begin{equation}\label{thin5}
H \bigl({\mathcal L} \bigl(B_{n,k}
\varepsilon_{(V_{n,k},Z_{n,k})} \bigr),{\mathcal L} (\widehat
N_{n,k} ) \bigr)  \le H({\mathcal L}(B_{n,k}),{\mathcal L}(\tau_{n,k})) .
\end{equation}

As $H({\mathcal L}(B_{n,k}),{\mathcal L}(\tau_{n,k}))\le3^{1/2}p_n$ (see
\cite{Re93}, Theorem 1.3.1(ii)), it follows from
(\ref{thin1})--(\ref{thin5}) and~(\ref{lre}) that


\begin{equation}\label{thin6}
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\|{\mathcal L}(\tilde N_n)-{\mathcal L}(\hat
N_n)\| \le \limsup_{n\to\infty}(3np_n^2)^{1/2}=0 .
\end{equation}

In view of a well-known upper bound of the laws of Poisson point
measures in terms of the corresponding intensity measures (see
\cite{Re93}, Section 3.2, equation (3.8)), it follows from (\ref{lre})
and $\|\ell\otimes Q\|=1$ that

\begin{eqnarray*}\label{thin7}
\|{\mathcal L}(\widehat N_n)-{\mathcal L}(N)\| & \le&
3\|\gamma\ell\otimes Q-np_n\ell\otimes Q_n\|\\
& \le& 3 |np_n-\gamma| + 3 np_n \|Q-Q_n\| \to0\qquad \mbox{as }
n\to\infty .
\end{eqnarray*}

By means of (\ref{thin6}) and (\ref{thin7}), this completes the proof
of the lemma.
